company_name: Companhia de Saneamento Básico do Estado de São Paulo (SABESP)

inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2025 ADJUSTED net revenue (20-F FY2025 Item 5: operating revenue excluding IFRIC 12 construction revenue of R$14,437.4m and the IPCA accretion on the bifurcated concession financial asset, ~R$1,442m). Reported revenue in the Metrics CSV (R$38,092m) includes construction revenue, a zero-margin pass-through equal to concession capex; projecting it would make revenue fall when the capex supercycle ends. All margin, D&A and capex paths below are percentages of ADJUSTED revenue. FY2024 adjusted comparable was R$21,725.8m (+2.2% in FY2025); H1 2026 adjusted +~9% y/y (Q1 +11%, Q2 +6.7%).
inputs.share_count_basis: Weighted average common shares adjusted for the dilutive effect, 6-K Q2-2026 Note 29: 3,523,860,958 (post 1:5 split; 3,524,534,026 issued at 30-Jun-2026 less treasury). The step from 3,417.5M to 3,523.9M in 2026 is the EMAE acquisition paid in shares (non-SBC issuance, already in the count). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows and the plan is settled from treasury shares.
inputs.net_debt_note: Company definition, consolidated 30-Jun-2026 (6-K Q2-2026 Note 5 capital management): total borrowings and financing R$51,657.8m less cash R$4,243.5m less financial investments R$13,197.4m = R$34,216.9m. `cash` here is cash + financial investments so that total_debt - cash ties to net_debt. Gross debt is ~R$10.6bn foreign-currency (partly swapped); covenant ceiling net debt/adjusted EBITDA 3.5x vs ~2.3x now.
inputs.interest_income_note: Income on financial investments FY2025 (20-F Note 33, R$1,347.0m) -- the yield on the R$13.2bn financial-investment pile that is netted in net_debt, so it is stripped from the owner-FCF anchor. The separate 'Interest income' line (R$456.1m) is customer-instalment interest and is operating; left in.
inputs.sbc_source: 20-F FY2025 cash flow statement share-based payment add-back (R$30.2m; the plan started April 2025; Note 29 of 6-K Q2-2026 shows R$64.6m for H1 2026, i.e. ~0.5% of adjusted revenue run-rate). No separate equity-award tax line; the plan is settled in treasury shares. Buyback FY2025 R$475.4m funded the treasury stock.
inputs.fx_note: USD/BRL 5.2223 (Yahoo BRL=X, 2026-10-02 close), i.e. 0.19149 USD per BRL applied model -> quote. 1 ADS = 1 common share after the 1:5 split (effective April 2026, ADS ratio restated). Parity check at the FX date: B3 close for SBSP3 x 0.19149 = US$5.41 against the NYSE ADR close, a 0.5% tie that confirms the rate direction and the 1:1 ADS ratio. The rate is dated; refresh_price.py moves the ADR price but not the rate.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in the flows' own currency, nominal BRL. Risk-free 10.0% = normalised BRL 10y (spot NTN-F ~13.5% with Selic at a 15% cyclical peak; 7-9% in 2020-21; BCB neutral real rate ~5% + 3% target + term premium). ERP 5.5%, beta 0.70 (regulated water monopoly, low cyclicality, but Brazilian political/regulatory beta) -> cost of equity ~13.9%. Cost of debt: debentures price at CDI+0.6-1.2% / IPCA+6.5-7.5%, normalised ~11.5% pre-tax, 7.6% after the 34% shield. Target D/V 35% (net debt/EBITDA guided toward ~2.5-3x) -> WACC 11.6%, rounded to 11.5%. Terminal growth 4.5% nominal = ~3.5% long-run IPCA + ~1% real (population, volume, RAB). The 7.0% spread is a touch harsher than a USD build (~9% WACC vs ~2.5% g) and is deliberate for Brazil. Same WACC in all three scenarios: regulatory, leverage and execution risk are charged ONCE, in the flows and the 25% bear weight, not again in the discount rate. For reference ARSESP's regulatory WACC is ~8.1% real, ~12% nominal; a model at the regulatory WACC values the RAB at ~1x by construction.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A), leases as debt: IFRS 16 lease liabilities are ~R$0.2bn (6-K Q2-2026 Note 14, total leases and right-of-use R$196m) against R$51.7bn of borrowings -- immaterial. No lease charge in the flows; lease renewal sits inside capex.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interest (EMAE, acquired 2026) was R$17m of H1 2026 profit -- immaterial. Flows treated as 100% attributable; no NCI deduction in the bridge.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (dcf-methods routing: non-US regulated operating company -> owner-fcf.md + adaptations a/b/c/d). A regulated concession is still a stream of unlevered cash flows; the capex supercycle (R$70bn 2024-2029 toward 99% water / 90% sewage by 2029) is modelled explicitly through the capex path -- year 1 is deeply negative, FCF normalises from 2027 as capex falls toward maintenance -- rather than anchored on a trough or on FY2024. FY2024 is NOT a base year (R$9.15bn non-cash concession financial-asset remeasurement gain at privatisation sits in revenue, EBITDA and net income). FY2025 reported FCF of -R$5.4bn is a supercycle year (capex R$13.7bn vs R$8.0bn), not a run-rate. REVENUE BASIS: adjusted revenue (ex IFRIC 12 construction revenue, ex IPCA accretion on the concession financial asset); the dashboard's historical revenue series (reported, incl. construction) will therefore sit above the projection's starting point -- that is the pass-through, not a forecast cut. EBITDA margins are on adjusted revenue: FY2025 ~60% (reported EBITDA R$14,808m less ~R$1,442m accretion over R$22,213m), Q1 2026 adjusted 63%, Q2 2026 ~60% after the Jaguaré incident. The concession financial asset (R$22.9bn indemnity receivable at end of concession 2060, indexed to IPCA only) is added in the equity bridge at its house-discounted value since its accretion is stripped from the flows. Future capex that will accrue to that asset is charged in the flows but its 2060 indemnity is not credited -- a conservative omission. 10-year horizon: the owner-FCF margin is still ramping through 2030 as capex normalises. SBC is small (0.5% of adjusted revenue) so the house/street band is narrow. Buyback (R$475m FY2025) funds the treasury shares used to settle SBC, so the flat count is being paid for. Cash tax rate 30% vs 34% statutory: interest on equity (JCP) is deductible and SABESP distributes through it (R$2.0bn JCP declared Dec-2025); H1 2026 effective 28-32%, FY2025 cash taxes R$2.5bn. Working-capital capture -8% of the revenue change (receivables ~17% of adjusted revenue, partly offset by payables).

equity_bridge.item: Concession financial asset (indemnity receivable from the grantor at end of concession, 2060) at house PV
equity_bridge.note: Book R$22,862m at 30-Jun-2026 (6-K Q2-2026 balance sheet, 'Financial Asset (Indemnity)'). Accretes at IPCA only (no real return) and is settled in 2060; its accretion revenue (~R$1.4bn/yr) is excluded from the adjusted revenue base. Matching-asset rule: value = 22,862 x ((1+0.045)/(1+0.115))^34 = R$2,520m. Booking it at face would be R$6.5/share of value that does not arrive for 34 years.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FY2026 adjusted-revenue run-rate (H1 2026 +~9% y/y: 9.9% tariff phase-in, +1% volume, adverse mix) and the RAB-remuneration ramp as the R$70bn programme enters the tariff base; NOT the equity CAGR
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR 15.8% vs revenue 20.0% and EPS 39.3%: the divergence exceeds 30% and every one of these series is distorted. Reported revenue CAGRs are inflated by IFRIC 12 construction revenue (R$5.6bn FY2023 -> R$14.4bn FY2025) -- adjusted revenue grew only 2.2% in FY2025. EPS and equity CAGRs carry the FY2024 R$9.15bn non-cash remeasurement gain and the FY2020 COVID trough base (EPS R$0.285). None is a usable forward anchor; selected growth is judgment on the regulated revenue build.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF CAGRs are undefined: the owner-FCF series (reported FCF less SBC less interest on financial investments) is R$1,474m FY2020, R$21m FY2021, R$148m FY2022, R$460m FY2023, -R$891m FY2024, -R$6,757m FY2025 -- the capex supercycle (R$3.3bn -> R$13.7bn) swamps it. SBC was zero until April 2025, so SBC-adjusted and reported FCF histories coincide before FY2025.

base.growth_note: Nominal BRL, adjusted revenue. 2026: H1 run-rate ~9% (9.9% tariff phase-in). 2027-2030: ~10%/yr = ~4.5% IPCA indexation + ~5% real as the R$50bn+ of net new RAB earns the regulatory return (ARSESP ~8.1% real pre-tax on an incremental R$50bn is ~R$4bn of revenue requirement plus depreciation), captured via annual adjustments and the 2029/30 periodic review. 2031+: decelerates to 5% nominal (3.5% inflation + 1-1.5% volume/new units) as universalization completes.
base.margin_note: FY2025 adjusted ~60%; Q1 2026 63%, Q2 2026 ~60% (Jaguaré, chemicals inflation). Expands because RAB-remuneration revenue is near-100% incremental margin while opex (~R$8.9bn FY2025) grows ~7%/yr nominal (inflation + 41% more sewage treatment capacity by 2029), and Equatorial's efficiency programme (headcount -12% y/y, free-market power, G&A) continues. Matures at 67%.
base.da_note: FY2025 D&A R$2,209m = 9.9% of adjusted revenue; H1 2026 R$1,435m -> ~12% run-rate as commissioned assets amortise over the concession to 2060. Rises to 14% as the R$70bn programme enters service.
base.capex_note: 2026: management guides 'close to R$20bn' (6-K Q2-2026 CEO letter) = ~82% of ~R$24.2bn adjusted revenue. The R$70bn 2024-2029 plan (20-F) less ~R$42bn spent 2024-2026 leaves ~R$28bn for 2027-2029: modelled R$10.1bn, R$9.4bn, R$9.0bn (38/32/28%). Post-2029 maintenance-plus-growth settles at 23% of revenue vs 14% D&A -- the ~9pt net investment funds RAB growth at roughly inflation. Pre-privatisation SABESP ran capex at ~20-24% of revenue (FY2016-FY2022).
base.tax_note: 34% statutory less the interest-on-equity (JCP) deduction; H1 2026 effective 28-32%. Applied to unlevered EBIT; the interest shield is in the WACC.
base.narrative: Base case: universalization delivered roughly on the 2029 schedule, the R$70bn programme lands close to plan with a modest tail, ARSESP's new DRC methodology and the periodic review remunerate the enlarged RAB at the regulatory return, and Equatorial's efficiency programme lifts adjusted EBITDA margins from ~60% to ~67% by 2030. Owner FCF is -R$8bn in 2026, turns positive in 2027 as capex halves, and reaches a mature ~28-30% margin by the mid-2030s.

bull.narrative: Bull case: the privatisation thesis plays out in full -- opex savings run ahead of the regulatory allowance and are retained between reviews, taking adjusted EBITDA margins to ~70% (Equatorial-distributor territory); the tariff review fully remunerates the new RAB with the U/Q factors earned rather than forfeited; the programme comes in on budget so capex drops to ~20% of revenue post-2029; Selic normalises toward 10%, pulling the cost of CDI-linked debt down. Value from a lower discount rate is NOT in this scenario -- WACC is held at the house rate -- so the bull case is operational, not a rates bet.

bear.narrative: Bear case: the programme overruns (~R$90bn rather than R$70bn, capex stays above R$12bn/yr through 2029), universalization targets slip and Factor U/Q penalties plus an unfavourable DRC methodology hold tariff growth to little more than inflation; opex inflation (chemicals, energy, treatment volumes) absorbs the efficiency gains so margins stall at ~61%; a slice of the R$18.2bn legal-contingency book crystallises; leverage approaches the 3.5x covenant and dividend capacity is squeezed. Net debt carries from a 2026-27 trough in FCF well above today's R$34bn. Owner FCF stays negative through 2027 and never exceeds a ~20% margin.

scenario_narratives.base: Universalization on schedule, R$70bn programme broadly on plan, enlarged RAB remunerated at the regulatory return from 2027-2030, Equatorial efficiency takes adjusted EBITDA margin from ~60% to 67%; FCF negative in 2026, positive from 2027, mature ~28-30% margin by the mid-2030s.
scenario_narratives.bull: Efficiency gains retained between reviews push margins to ~70%, U/Q factors earned, programme on budget so capex falls to ~20% of revenue post-2029, Selic normalises; an operational bull case with WACC held at the house rate.
scenario_narratives.bear: Programme overruns to ~R$90bn, targets slip and Factor U/Q penalties bite, DRC methodology unfavourable, opex inflation stalls margins at ~61%, contingencies crystallise, leverage heads toward the 3.5x covenant; FCF negative through 2027.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: a single-regulator dependency (ARSESP sets every tariff, DRC methodology under consultation), net debt doubling into a 15% Selic environment with R$40-50bn more to raise, Factor U/Q penalties on a 2029 deadline, and R$18.2bn of contingencies against R$1.9bn provisioned. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: it needs several independent things to go right at once -- retained efficiency gains, a generous periodic review, an on-budget programme and lower rates -- in a jurisdiction where the State keeps a golden share and an 18% stake. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: SABESP is valued as what it is after privatisation: a regulated monopoly concession to 2060 in the middle of a debt-funded capex supercycle. The house owner-FCF DCF charges that supercycle explicitly (year-1 FCF of roughly -R$8bn), normalises capex toward maintenance from 2027, lets the enlarged regulated asset base earn its return through the tariff, and discounts nominal BRL flows at a nominal BRL WACC with risk charged once. The value is terminal-heavy and therefore discount-rate-heavy: the required-return table is the honest reading of what the ADR price implies. A USD-based ADR holder additionally bears BRL depreciation, which the BRL WACC (not the fx_rate) is where that lives.
key_risks_to_valuation: Discount rate: ~70%+ of value is terminal; each 1pt of nominal BRL WACC moves value per share by roughly a quarter. The market appears to be capitalising SABESP nearer a 10% nominal BRL rate than the house 11.5%.

Revenue basis: the model projects ADJUSTED revenue (ex IFRIC 12 construction revenue, ex financial-asset accretion). If a reader compares the projection with the CSV's reported revenue they will see a R$14bn gap that is the construction pass-through, not a forecast.

Capex normalisation: the base case has capex falling from ~R$20bn (2026) to ~R$9-10bn (2027-2029) per the R$70bn plan. If the plan is extended or overruns, the FCF inflection moves right by a year or more (bear case).
Tariff recognition lag: RAB remuneration arrives through annual adjustments and the periodic review; the base case smooths it at ~10%/yr 2027-2030, the actual path will be lumpier.
Concession financial asset is in the bridge at R$2.5bn (house PV), not its R$22.9bn book; a reader using book would add ~R$5.8/share (~US$1.10).
FX: all values are built in BRL and converted at a dated spot rate; a 10% BRL move is a 10% move in the USD intrinsic value with nothing changing in the business.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API for the NYSE ADR at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 4.43-7.16; FX from Yahoo BRL=X at the same date; B3 SBSP3 close used as the parity check (see inputs.fx_note)
data_sources.financials: SBS_Metrics.csv (core_metrics, BRL millions, FY2016-FY2025 + Q1-Q2 2026); 20-F FY2025 (Item 5 adjusted revenue R$22,213.0m and construction revenue R$14,437.4m; Note 33 income on financial investments; Note 29 diluted shares; capex plan R$70bn 2024-2029); 6-K Q2-2026 (Note 5 net debt R$34,216.9m consolidated; balance sheet financial asset R$22,862m; Note 29 share-based payment and diluted shares 3,523,860,958; CEO letter capex ~R$20bn FY2026; adjusted net revenue +6.7%)
data_sources.qualitative: SBS_Analysis.json (2026-10-04): URAE-1 concession to 2060, 99%/90% universalization by 2029, Factor U/Q tariff mechanics, Equatorial control, R$18.2bn contingencies, leverage trajectory
